questions.story:
"The Projection Room at the Roxy"

Passage 1
Mr Okonkwo had looked after the two projectors at the Roxy for twenty-six years. He cleaned the gates between every showing and could hear a misaligned sprocket from the far side of the room. He kept the lenses in a felt-lined case that nobody else was permitted to open. No reel had ever jammed during a performance, not once in all that time. He spoke to the machines under his breath while he worked, and the ushers had long since stopped remarking on it.

Passage 2
The staff had learned to leave the projection room alone. Young Petra carried the reels only as far as the top step and set them down there. The Roxy had opened in 1937 and still had its original velvet seats. The manager sent messages up by note rather than climbing the stairs himself. Even the cleaners worked around the room, sweeping the corridor and going no further.

Passage 3
Only Delia, who sold tickets in the front booth, ever went into the projection room. She came and went as she pleased, sometimes staying through a whole showing. ____________________ Mr Okonkwo had never once objected to any of it, and nobody else in the building could say why she alone was allowed.

Passage 4
The arrangement held quietly until the autumn. Then one Tuesday the felt-lined lens case was not in its place on the shelf. Mr Okonkwo searched the projection room twice and asked every member of staff in turn. The Roxy stood on the corner of Harrow Lane and had a curved art deco frontage. It had been built as a dance hall and converted to a cinema three years later. The plasterwork above the screen was original and had never been repainted.

Passage 5
Delia was the last person he asked, and she gave him no answer at all. She only turned back to the ledger of ticket stubs in front of her and went on counting. It was then that Mr Okonkwo noticed the edge of grey felt showing beneath the counter, and beside it the small lens brush he had not been able to find since the spring.
question: Read passage no. 1. What is the topic of this passage?

options.text: The history of the Roxy cinema and how it came to be built
The duties carried out by the ushers and the cleaning staff
Mr Okonkwo’s meticulous care of the two projectors
The films that were shown at the Roxy across twenty-six years
